title: Cuba Crises Update — May 12, 2026
summary: Nine new events document Cuba's deepening crisis from April 18 to May 9, 2026: a high-level US delegation visited Havana in the first such visit since Obama, but talks failed to break the stalemate over the oil blockade. Cuba's energy minister warned that Russian fuel reserves were exhausted, pushing the generation deficit above 1,400 MW with blackouts reaching 20–24 hours daily. Secretary Rubio declared economic reforms 'impossible' under Díaz-Canel — who defiantly told NBC he would not step down. Over 500,000 marched in Havana on May Day, and Cuba unveiled a new migration law allowing diaspora investment while its private sector faced collapse. Venezuela oil import data and the informal exchange rate were updated to reflect the oil blockade's impact; two energy infrastructure map points added.
